name: Gentamicin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside cleared by glomerular filtration; it is nephrotoxic and ototoxic (boxed warning), with higher risk in kidney impairment. The US label adjusts by serum creatinine (interval = serum creatinine × 8 hours, or a reduced-dose table) with serum-level monitoring, and gives 1 to 1.7 mg/kg at the end of each hemodialysis (2 mg/kg in children). Peritoneal dialysis removes it much more slowly than hemodialysis.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses serum creatinine (mg/dL) with an approximate CrCl (mL/min/1.73 m2) table.

bands.recommendation: Normal kidney function: 3 mg/kg/day in 3 doses every 8 hours; up to 5 mg/kg/day for life-threatening infection, reduced as soon as possible. Obese patients: dose by lean body mass. Measure peaks (4 to 6 mcg/mL) and troughs (label).

After the usual first dose, either extend the interval (hours = serum creatinine in mg/dL × 8) or keep 8-hourly doses reduced by the label's serum creatinine table (Table 4) or by dividing the normal dose by serum creatinine. Avoid prolonged peaks above 12 mcg/mL and troughs above 2 mcg/mL; measure levels (label). Table 4 example: serum creatinine 1.4–1.6 mg/dL (CrCl about 55–70): 65% of the usual dose every 8 hours.

Avoid prolonged peaks above 12 mcg/mL and troughs above 2 mcg/mL; measure levels (label). Table 4 example: CrCl about 20–25: 25%; 15–20: 20% of the usual dose every 8 hours.

After the usual first dose, either extend the interval (hours = serum creatinine in mg/dL × 8) or keep 8-hourly doses reduced by the label's serum creatinine table (Table 4) or by dividing the normal dose by serum creatinine. Avoid prolonged peaks above 12 mcg/mL and troughs above 2 mcg/mL; measure levels (label). Table 4: CrCl about 10–15: 15%; under 10: 10% of the usual dose every 8 hours. Specialist input.

hd: 1 to 1.7 mg/kg at the end of each dialysis, depending on severity of infection; an 8-hour hemodialysis lowers levels by about 50% (label). Check levels.
pd: No PD dose in label; removal by peritoneal dialysis is much slower than by hemodialysis. For PD peritonitis, intraperitoneal dosing per the ISPD 2022 guideline; specialist input.
crrt: No data in label, and gentamicin is not in the Li 2020 CRRT table. Level-guided dosing with specialist input.
dialyzable: Yes by hemodialysis (about 50% over 8 hours; label); much less by peritoneal dialysis. Protein binding 0% to 30%.
monitoring: Peak and trough levels; serum creatinine before and during therapy; urinalysis; hearing and vestibular function; magnesium, calcium and potassium (wasting, Fanconi-like syndrome reported). Avoid other nephrotoxic drugs and potent diuretics.

pediatric.approved_ages: Children, infants and neonates (label; this premixed bag may not suit small children).
pediatric.usual_dose: Children: 6 to 7.5 mg/kg/day (2 to 2.5 mg/kg every 8 hours). Infants and neonates: 7.5 mg/kg/day (2.5 mg/kg every 8 hours) (label).
pediatric.neonates: Premature or full-term neonates 1 week of age or less: 5 mg/kg/day (2.5 mg/kg every 12 hours) (label).

renal.recommendation: Label serum creatinine methods are not age-limited; monitor levels. Specialist input in children.

pediatric.hd: Children: 2 mg/kg at the end of each dialysis (label). Check levels.
pediatric.pd: No label dose; see ISPD 2022; specialist.

adult: Selected label is the Baxter premixed bag (2023); PH products are 40 mg/mL vials (plus ophthalmic/otic drops and cream). Kidney dosing is the same drug; consider pinning a vial label with pediatric 10 mg/mL text.
Label describes conventional 8-hourly dosing; extended-interval dosing is not in the label.
ISPD 2022 intraperitoneal gentamicin dose not stated (full text not read).
pediatric: Serum creatinine × 8 and Table 4 were derived in adults; a child's lower creatinine makes them less reliable. Kept as label wording.
